sanskrit: śūlapāṇir ivākṣobhyo varuṇaḥ pāśavān iva yugāntāgnir ivārciṣmān pradhakṣyan vai punaḥ prajāḥ
english: Unshakable like the trident-bearer Śiva, like Varuṇa armed with his nooses, blazing like the fire at the end of an age about to burn up all creatures once more,

sanskrit: krodhāmarṣabaloddhūto nivātakavacāntakaḥ jayo jetā sthitaḥ satye pārayiṣyan mahāvratam
english: surging with the strength of wrath and indignation, the slayer of the Nivātakavacas, victory itself and the conqueror, firm in truth and resolved to carry his great vow through to its end,

sanskrit: āmuktakavacaḥ khaḍgī jāmbūnadakirīṭabhṛt śubhravarmāmbaradharaḥ svaṅgadī cārukuṇḍalī
english: his armor donned, his sword girt on, wearing a diadem of pure gold, clad in shining mail and raiment, with fair armlets and lovely earrings—

sanskrit: rathapravaram āsthāya naro nārāyaṇānugaḥ vidhunvan gāṇḍivaṃ saṃkhye babhau sūrya ivoditaḥ
english: Nara, the follower of Nārāyaṇa, mounting his peerless chariot and brandishing the Gāṇḍīva in battle, shone like the risen sun.

sanskrit: so 'grānīkasya mahata iṣupāte dhanaṃjayaḥ vyavasthāpya rathaṃ sajjaṃ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān
english: Within bowshot of that great vanguard, the valiant Dhanaṃjaya, having drawn up his ready chariot, blew his conch.

sanskrit: atha kṛṣṇo 'py asaṃbhrāntaḥ pārthena saha māriṣa prādhmāpayat pāñcajanyaṃ śaṅkhapravaram ojasā
english: Then Kṛṣṇa too, unflurried, together with Pārtha, O honored one, blew with all his might the Pāñcajanya, finest of conches.

sanskrit: tayoḥ śaṅkhapraṇādena tava sainye viśāṃ pate āsan saṃhṛṣṭaromāṇaḥ kampitā gatacetasaḥ
english: At the blare of their conches, O lord of peoples, the men of your army bristled with horror, trembled, and lost their senses.

sanskrit: yathā trasanti bhūtāni sarvāṇy aśaninisvanāt tathā śaṅkhapraṇādena vitresus tava sainikāḥ
english: As all living things shudder at the crash of a thunderbolt, so at the blare of those conches your soldiers were seized with fear.

sanskrit: prasusruvuḥ śakṛnmūtraṃ vāhanāni ca sarvaśaḥ evaṃ savāhanaṃ sarvam āvignam abhavad balam
english: The beasts of burden everywhere let flow their dung and urine; thus the whole host, mounts and all, was thrown into turmoil.

sanskrit: vyaṣīdanta narā rājañ śaṅkhaśabdena māriṣa visaṃjñāś cābhavan ke cit ke cid rājan vitatrasuḥ
english: The men sank down, O king, at the sound of the conch, O honored one; some fell senseless, and others, O king, were struck with terror.

sanskrit: tataḥ kapir mahānādaṃ saha bhūtair dhvajālayaiḥ akarod vyāditāsyaś ca bhīṣayaṃs tava sainikān
english: Then the ape upon the banner, with the spirits that dwelt in it, raised a great roar with gaping jaws, terrifying your soldiers.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca mṛdaṅgāś cānakaiḥ saha punar evābhyahanyanta tava sainyapraharṣaṇāḥ
english: Then conches and kettledrums and tabors, together with the war-drums, were struck up once more to hearten your troops.

sanskrit: nānāvāditrasaṃhrādaiḥ kṣveḍitāsphoṭitākulaiḥ siṃhanādaiḥ savāditraiḥ samāhūtair mahārathaiḥ
english: With the din of manifold instruments, with the tumult of shouts and the slapping of arms, with lions' roars mingled with music, the great chariot-warriors challenged one another.

sanskrit: tasmin sutumule śabde bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhane atīva hṛṣṭo dāśārham abravīt pākaśāsaniḥ
english: Amid that wild uproar, which swelled the dread of cowards, the son of Indra, exceedingly elated, spoke to the Dāśārha:

sanskrit: codayāśvān hṛṣīkeśa yatra durmarṣaṇaḥ sthitaḥ etad bhittvā gajānīkaṃ pravekṣyāmy arivāhinīm
english: "Drive on the horses, Hṛṣīkeśa, to where Durmarṣaṇa stands. Breaking through this elephant-host, I will plunge into the enemy's army."

sanskrit: evam ukto mahābāhuḥ keśavaḥ savyasācinā acodayad dhayāṃs tatra yatra durmarṣaṇaḥ sthitaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Savyasācin, mighty-armed Keśava urged the horses on to where Durmarṣaṇa stood.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulaḥ saṃpravṛttaḥ sudāruṇaḥ ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca rathanāganarakṣayaḥ
english: Then there began a tumultuous and most terrible clash—between one man and many—a slaughter of chariots, elephants, and men.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāyakavarṣeṇa parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān parān avākirat pārthaḥ parvatān iva nīradaḥ
english: Then Pārtha, with a downpour of arrows, like the rain-cloud Parjanya pouring water, drenched his foes as a cloud drenches the mountains.

sanskrit: te cāpi rathinaḥ sarve tvaritāḥ kṛtahastavat avākiran bāṇajālais tataḥ kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau
english: And all those chariot-warriors too, swift and deft of hand, covered Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya with nets of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahābāhur vāryamāṇaḥ parair yudhi śirāṃsi rathināṃ pārthaḥ kāyebhyo 'pāharac charaiḥ
english: Then the mighty-armed Pārtha, enraged, though held in check by his foes in the fight, struck the heads of the chariot-warriors from their bodies with his shafts.

sanskrit: udbhrāntanayanair vaktraiḥ saṃdaṣṭoṣṭhapuṭaiḥ śubhaiḥ sakuṇḍalaśirastrāṇair vasudhā samakīryata
english: The earth was strewn with handsome faces, their eyes rolling and their lips bitten, still wearing their earrings and helmets.

sanskrit: puṇḍarīkavanānīva vidhvastāni samantataḥ vinikīrṇāni yodhānāṃ vadanāni cakāśire
english: Scattered all about, the faces of the warriors gleamed like beds of white lotuses laid waste on every side.

sanskrit: tapanīyavicitrāṇi siktāni rudhireṇa ca adṛśyanta yathā rājan meghasaṃghāḥ savidyutaḥ
english: Bright with golden ornaments and bathed in blood, they looked, O king, like masses of cloud lit by lightning.

sanskrit: śirasāṃ patatāṃ rājañ śabdo 'bhūt pṛthivītale kālena paripakvānāṃ tālānāṃ patatām iva
english: The sound of the heads falling upon the ground, O king, was like that of ripe palmyra fruits dropping in their season.

sanskrit: tataḥ kabandhaḥ kaś cit tu dhanur ālambya tiṣṭhati kaś cit khaḍgaṃ viniṣkṛṣya bhujenodyamya tiṣṭhati
english: Then here a headless trunk stood propped upon its bow, and there another stood with its sword drawn and raised aloft in its arm.

sanskrit: nājānanta śirāṃsy urvyāṃ patitāni nararṣabhāḥ amṛṣyamāṇāḥ kaunteyaṃ saṃgrāme jayagṛddhinaḥ
english: Those bulls among men did not even know their own heads had fallen to the earth—still unable to brook the son of Kuntī, still craving victory in the fight.

sanskrit: hayānām uttamāṅgaiś ca hastihastaiś ca medinī bāhubhiś ca śirobhiś ca vīrāṇāṃ samakīryata
english: The earth was strewn with the heads of horses and the trunks of elephants, and with the arms and heads of heroes.

sanskrit: ayaṃ pārthaḥ kutaḥ pārtha eṣa pārtha iti prabho tava sainyeṣu yodhānāṃ pārthabhūtam ivābhavat
english: "Here is Pārtha! Where is Pārtha? This is Pārtha!"—so, O lord, among your troops it was as if the warriors saw nothing but Pārtha everywhere.

sanskrit: anyonyam api cājaghnur ātmānam api cāpare pārthabhūtam amanyanta jagat kālena mohitāḥ
english: They even struck down one another, and some struck down themselves, deeming the whole world to have become Pārtha, deluded as they were by Time.

sanskrit: niṣṭanantaḥ sarudhirā visaṃjñā gāḍhavedanāḥ śayānā bahavo vīrāḥ kīrtayantaḥ suhṛjjanam
english: Many heroes lay there, moaning and bloodied, senseless and in sharp pain, calling out the names of their dear ones.

sanskrit: sabhiṇḍipālāḥ saprāsāḥ saśaktyṛṣṭiparaśvadhāḥ saniryūhāḥ sanistriṃśāḥ saśarāsanatomarāḥ
english: With slings and javelins, with lances, pikes, and battle-axes, with maces and swords, with bows and iron darts—

sanskrit: sabāṇavarmābharaṇāḥ sagadāḥ sāṅgadā raṇe mahābhujagasaṃkāśā bāhavaḥ parighopamāḥ
english: with arrows, armor, and ornaments, with clubs, still bearing their armlets in battle, arms like great serpents, like iron bludgeons,

sanskrit: udveṣṭanti viceṣṭanti saṃveṣṭanti ca sarvaśaḥ vegaṃ kurvanti saṃrabdhā nikṛttāḥ parameṣubhiḥ
english: writhed and twitched and curled in every direction, jerking in fury though severed by his keenest shafts.

sanskrit: yo yaḥ sma samare pārthaṃ pratisaṃrabhate naraḥ tasya tasyāntako bāṇaḥ śarīram upasarpati
english: Whatever man in the battle set himself in fury against Pārtha, upon that man's body an arrow crept like death itself.

sanskrit: nṛtyato rathamārgeṣu dhanur vyāyacchatas tathā na kaś cit tatra pārthasya dadarśāntaram aṇv api
english: As he danced along the chariot-tracks and bent his bow, not one there could spy in Pārtha even the smallest opening.

sanskrit: yat tasya ghaṭamānasya kṣipraṃ vikṣipataḥ śarān lāghavāt pāṇḍuputrasya vyasmayanta pare janāḥ
english: At the deftness with which the son of Pāṇḍu, striving hard, loosed his arrows so swiftly, the enemy host stood amazed.

sanskrit: hastinaṃ hastiyantāram aśvam āśvikam eva ca abhinat phalguno bāṇai rathinaṃ ca sasārathim
english: Elephant and elephant-driver, horse and horseman alike, and chariot-warrior together with his charioteer—Phalguna pierced them all with his arrows.

sanskrit: āvartamānam āvṛttaṃ yudhyamānaṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ pramukhe tiṣṭhamānaṃ ca na kaṃ cin na nihanti saḥ
english: Whoever wheeled about, whoever had turned away, whoever stood and fought, whoever stood before him in the van—there was none the Pāṇḍava did not slay.

sanskrit: yathodayan vai gagane sūryo hanti mahat tamaḥ tathārjuno gajānīkam avadhīt kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: As the rising sun in the sky dispels the great darkness, so did Arjuna destroy the elephant-host with his heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: hastibhiḥ patitair bhinnais tava sainyam adṛśyata antakāle yathā bhūmir vinikīrṇair mahīdharaiḥ
english: With elephants fallen and shattered, your army looked like the earth at the end of time, strewn with mountains overthrown.

sanskrit: yathā madhyaṃdine sūryo duṣprekṣyaḥ prāṇibhiḥ sadā tathā dhanaṃjayaḥ kruddho duṣprekṣyo yudhi śatrubhiḥ
english: As the noonday sun is ever hard for living things to gaze upon, so was the wrathful Dhanaṃjaya hard for his foes to look upon in battle.

sanskrit: tat tathā tava putrasya sainyaṃ yudhi paraṃtapa prabhagnaṃ drutam āvignam atīva śarapīḍitam
english: Thus, O scorcher of foes, was your son's army in the fight broken, routed, thrown into utter disorder, and grievously tormented by arrows.

sanskrit: māruteneva mahatā meghānīkaṃ vidhūyatā prakālyamānaṃ tat sainyaṃ nāśakat prativīkṣitum
english: That army, driven before him like a mass of clouds scattered by a mighty wind, could not so much as look upon him.

sanskrit: pratodaiś cāpakoṭībhir huṃkāraiḥ sādhuvāhitaiḥ kaśāpārṣṇyabhighātaiś ca vāgbhir ugrābhir eva ca
english: With goads and with the tips of their bows, with shouts and well-trained urging, with the lash and the strike of the heel, and with harsh words besides,

sanskrit: codayanto hayāṃs tūrṇaṃ palāyante sma tāvakāḥ sādino rathinaś caiva pattayaś cārjunārditāḥ
english: driving their horses on in haste, your men took to flight—riders, chariot-warriors, and foot-soldiers alike, tormented by Arjuna.

sanskrit: pārṣṇyaṅguṣṭhāṅkuśair nāgāṃś codayantas tathāpare śaraiḥ saṃmohitāś cānye tam evābhimukhā yayau tava yodhā hatotsāhā vibhrāntamanasas tadā
english: Others spurred their elephants on with heel and toe and goad, while still others, stupefied by his arrows, were borne straight toward him—your warriors then, their spirit broken and their minds awhirl.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tasmin prabhagne sainyāgre vadhyamāne kirīṭinā ke nu tatra raṇe vīrāḥ pratyudīyur dhanaṃjayam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that vanguard of the army was broken and being slaughtered by the Diademed One, what heroes there in the battle went forth to meet Dhanaṃjaya?

sanskrit: āho svic chakaṭavyūhaṃ praviṣṭā moghaniścayāḥ droṇam āśritya tiṣṭhantaḥ prākāram akutobhayāḥ
english: Or had they, their resolve undone, withdrawn into the cart-array, taking refuge behind Droṇa as behind a rampart, free from any fear?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathārjunena saṃbhagne tasmiṃs tava bale tadā hatavīre hatotsāhe palāyanakṛtakṣaṇe
english: Saṃjaya said: When that host of yours had thus been shattered by Arjuna, its heroes slain, its spirit gone, watching only for the moment to flee,

sanskrit: pākaśāsaninābhīkṣṇaṃ vadhyamāne śarottamaiḥ na tatra kaś cit saṃgrāme śaśākārjunam īkṣitum
english: as it was struck again and again by the son of Indra with his finest shafts, no one there in the fight was able even to look upon Arjuna.

sanskrit: tatas tava suto rājan dṛṣṭvā sainyaṃ tathāgatam duḥśāsano bhṛśaṃ kruddho yuddhāyārjunam abhyayāt
english: Then your son Duḥśāsana, O king, seeing his army brought to such a pass, exceedingly enraged, advanced upon Arjuna to do battle.

sanskrit: sa kāñcanavicitreṇa kavacena samāvṛtaḥ jāmbūnadaśirastrāṇaḥ śūras tīvraparākramaḥ
english: Clad in armor wrought with gold, his helmet of pure gold, that hero of fierce prowess,

sanskrit: nāgānīkena mahatā grasann iva mahīm imām duḥśāsano mahārāja savyasācinam āvṛṇot
english: with a great host of elephants, as though devouring this very earth, Duḥśāsana, O great king, hemmed in Savyasācin.

sanskrit: hrādena gajaghaṇṭānāṃ śaṅkhānāṃ ninadena ca jyākṣepaninadaiś caiva virāveṇa ca dantinām
english: With the clamor of the elephants' bells, with the blaring of conches, with the twang of bowstrings, and with the trumpeting of the tuskers,

sanskrit: bhūr diśaś cāntarikṣaṃ ca śabdenāsīt samāvṛtam sa muhūrtaṃ pratibhayo dāruṇaḥ samapadyata
english: the earth, the quarters, and the sky were filled with the din; and for a moment it grew dreadful and terrifying.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā patatas tūrṇam aṅkuśair abhicoditān vyālambahastān saṃrabdhān sapakṣān iva parvatān
english: Seeing them rushing swiftly down, urged on by goads, their trunks swinging, furious, like winged mountains,

sanskrit: siṃhanādena mahatā narasiṃho dhanaṃjayaḥ gajānīkam amitrāṇām abhito vyadhamac charaiḥ
english: with a mighty lion's roar that man-lion Dhanaṃjaya scattered the elephant-host of his foes on every side with his arrows.

sanskrit: mahormiṇam ivoddhūtaṃ śvasanena mahārṇavam kirīṭī tad gajānīkaṃ prāviśan makaro yathā
english: Into that elephant-host, heaving with great waves like a vast ocean stirred up by the wind, the Diademed One plunged like a sea-monster.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhātīta ivādityaḥ pratapan yugasaṃkṣaye dadṛśe dikṣu sarvāsu pārthaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Like the sun blazing past its bounds at the dissolution of an age, Pārtha, conqueror of hostile cities, was seen in every quarter.

sanskrit: khuraśabdena cāśvānāṃ nemighoṣeṇa tena ca tena cotkruṣṭaśabdena jyāninādena tena ca devadattasya ghoṣeṇa gāṇḍīvaninadena ca
english: With the clatter of the horses' hooves and the rumble of the chariot-rims, with the uproar of shouting and the twang of the bowstring, with the blast of the Devadatta and the thunder of the Gāṇḍīva,

sanskrit: mandavegatarā nāgā babhūvus te vicetasaḥ śarair āśīviṣasparśair nirbhinnāḥ savyasācinā
english: those elephants grew sluggish and lost their wits, pierced through by Savyasācin with shafts whose touch was that of venomous serpents.

sanskrit: te gajā viśikhais tīkṣṇair yudhi gāṇḍīvacoditaiḥ anekaśatasāhasraiḥ sarvāṅgeṣu samarpitāḥ
english: Those elephants, struck in every limb by the sharp barbless shafts sped from the Gāṇḍīva in the fight, in their many hundreds of thousands,

sanskrit: ārāvaṃ paramaṃ kṛtvā vadhyamānāḥ kirīṭinā nipetur aniśaṃ bhūmau chinnapakṣā ivādrayaḥ
english: raising a tremendous outcry as they were slain by the Diademed One, fell ceaselessly to the earth like mountains with their wings shorn off.

sanskrit: apare dantaveṣṭeṣu kumbheṣu ca kaṭeṣu ca śaraiḥ samarpitā nāgāḥ krauñcavad vyanadan muhuḥ
english: Other elephants, struck by arrows in their tusk-sockets, their frontal bosses, and their temples, cried out again and again like the krauñca bird.

sanskrit: gajaskandhagatānāṃ ca puruṣāṇāṃ kirīṭinā ācchidyantottamāṅgāni bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: And the heads of the men mounted upon the elephants' shoulders were lopped off by the Diademed One with his broad-headed, smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalānāṃ patatāṃ śirasāṃ dharaṇītale padmānām iva saṃghātaiḥ pārthaś cakre nivedanam
english: With the masses of heads, still wearing their earrings, that fell to the ground like clusters of lotuses, Pārtha made, as it were, his offering.

sanskrit: yantrabaddhā vikavacā vraṇārtā rudhirokṣitāḥ bhramatsu yudhi nāgeṣu manuṣyā vilalambire
english: Lashed to their seats, stripped of armor, anguished with wounds and drenched in blood, men hung dangling upon the elephants as they wheeled about in the battle.

sanskrit: ke cid ekena bāṇena sumuktena patatriṇā dvau trayaś ca vinirbhinnā nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Some, two and three together, pierced through by a single well-loosed feathered shaft, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: maurvīṃ dhanur dhvajaṃ caiva yugānīṣās tathaiva ca rathināṃ kuṭṭayām āsa bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Bowstring and bow and banner, yokes and poles alike, of the chariot-warriors he hewed to pieces with his broad-headed, smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: na saṃdadhan na cāpy asyan na vimuñcan na coddharan maṇḍalenaiva dhanuṣā nṛtyan pārthaḥ sma dṛśyate
english: Not nocking, not aiming, not loosing, not drawing out—Pārtha was seen dancing, his bow bent into one continuous circle.

sanskrit: atividdhāś ca nārācair vamanto rudhiraṃ mukhaiḥ muhūrtān nipatanty anye vāraṇā vasudhātale
english: And other elephants, pierced deep by his iron shafts, vomiting blood from their mouths, in a moment fell to the earth.

sanskrit: utthitāny agaṇeyāni kabandhāni samantataḥ adṛśyanta mahārāja tasmin paramasaṃkule
english: Countless headless trunks were seen rising up on every side, O great king, in that supreme melee.

sanskrit: sacāpāḥ sāṅgulitrāṇāḥ sakhaḍgāḥ sāṅgadā raṇe adṛśyanta bhujāś chinnā hemābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: Severed arms, still grasping bows, still in their finger-guards, still gripping swords, still wearing their armlets and adorned with golden ornaments, were seen upon the field.

sanskrit: sūpaskarair adhiṣṭhānair īṣādaṇḍakabandhuraiḥ cakrair vimathitair akṣai bhagnaiś ca bahudhā yugaiḥ
english: With well-fitted frames and platforms, with poles, shafts, and chariot-floors, with wheels crushed and axles and yokes broken in many pieces,

sanskrit: varmacāpaśaraiś caiva vyavakīrṇais tatas tataḥ sragbhir ābharaṇair vastraiḥ patitaiś ca mahādhvajaiḥ
english: with armor, bows, and arrows scattered here and there, with garlands, ornaments, and garments, and with great banners fallen down,

sanskrit: nihatair vāraṇair aśvaiḥ kṣatriyaiś ca nipātitaiḥ adṛśyata mahī tatra dāruṇapratidarśanā
english: with elephants and horses slain and warriors struck down, the earth there appeared dreadful to behold.

sanskrit: evaṃ duḥśāsanabalaṃ vadhyamānaṃ kirīṭinā saṃprādravan mahārāja vyathitaṃ vai sanāyakam
english: Thus the army of Duḥśāsana, as it was being slaughtered by the Diademed One, fled away, O great king, sorely shaken, along with its leader.

sanskrit: tato duḥśāsanas trastaḥ sahānīkaḥ śarārditaḥ droṇaṃ trātāram ākāṅkṣañ śakaṭavyūham abhyagāt
english: Then Duḥśāsana, terrified, his force tormented by arrows, longing for Droṇa as his protector, made for the cart-array.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duḥśāsanabalaṃ hatvā savyasācī dhanaṃjayaḥ sindhurājaṃ parīpsan vai droṇānīkam upādravat
english: Saṃjaya said: Having struck down the host of Duḥśāsana, Savyasācin Dhanaṃjaya, eager to reach the king of the Sindhus, fell upon Droṇa's array.

sanskrit: sa tu droṇaṃ samāsādya vyūhasya pramukhe sthitam kṛtāñjalir idaṃ vākyaṃ kṛṣṇasyānumate 'bravīt
english: Then, coming upon Droṇa stationed at the head of the formation, he folded his hands in salutation and, with Kṛṣṇa's assent, spoke these words:
